newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Slow Australian stocks pare gains by close.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Slow Australian stocks pare gains by close.

text.p: *Stocks close just firmer, come off highs in afternoon as bellwether BHP fades. Volume 376.59 million, A$733.69 million value, 1,134 traded, 349 steady, 420 up, 365 down.
Australian shares closed just firmer on Thursday, the market sliding off its highs in the afternoon as bellwether BHP faded amid heavy options trade as the January series options reached expiry.
At 4.10 p.m. (0510 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was up 3.5 points at 2,417.7.
March share price index futures were six points higher at 2,413, a 4.7 point discount to the index.
The leaders turned in a mixed performance with brokers saying much of the activity was related to options positions rather than fresh corporate leads.
"Lots of the activity has because of the options," said a Sydney-based dealer, noting that the leaders were nearly always subject to choppy trade ahead of options expiries.
"There was a reasonable tone about it but they were always going to be moved about today."

Corporate news in the leaders was light but at the smaller end shares in biotech company Progen rocketed 20 percent to close at A$0.92 cents after it reported encouraging results from tests of its anti-cancer compound. Progen said the PI-88 compound inhibited the growth rate of human colon cancer in mice which had been transplanted with primary human tumours.
Gawler Craton gold hopeful Desertstone failed to fare as well. Its shares fell 47 percent to A$0.34 after its progress report on the Lake Torrens project failed to meet expectations.
In the second line banks, Bank of Melbourne shares soared nearly four percent to A$8.91 as takeover speculation stirred again ahead of the Wallis inquiry conclusion in March.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Futures trade was moderate, options trade boomed as the January series options expired.
Turnover in March SPI contracts totalled 5,040 (7,369)

In other local markets, Australian bonds finished firmer on renewed rate cut hopes after Wednesday's CPI data confirmed low inflation status. By 4.50 p.m. (0550 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.40 percent, down 0.07 from Wednesday.

The Australian dollar enjoyed a rare 1/2 cent rally as demand from respected Swiss and U.S. names caught the market in a classic bear squeeze. But again the currency was handicapped by the risk of a domestic rate cut and had yet to show the sort of revival that might presage an end to its two month-old downtrend. By 4.50 p.m. (0550 GMT), the unit was quoted at US$0.7707/12, up on US$0.7673/78 here Wednesday.
